definition: anything of the physical world: animals, plants, fungi and their parts and products; land, water, weather and sky; minerals, rocks, soils, metals and other substances and materials; colours, textures and physical properties; and the physical objects a person would hear as a thing of the world. A word belongs if a person would hear it as a thing of the world; persons, social, institutional, religious, abstract, medical and purely technical terms do not.

_provenance.themeDefinition: anything of the physical world - animals, plants, weather, land, materials, colours, textures; be generous inside that definition, the point is a mnemonic FLAVOUR, not a taxonomy; a word belongs if a person would hear it as a thing of the world

sourceDictionary.name: Apple macOS dictionary (web2, Webster's 1913 lineage)
sourceDictionary.role: reference dictionary: every shipped word appears exactly in it, checked with grep -x

semanticEvidence.name: Apple macOS Dictionary Services (New Oxford American Dictionary)
semanticEvidence.method: DCSCopyTextDefinition per word over all 103,788 lowercase 4-9 letter dictionary entries
semanticEvidence.role: classification evidence only: a word whose own definition names a physical-world head noun is admitted; nothing from it is shipped

rules.shape: lowercase a-z only, 4 to 9 letters, single word, no space or hyphen
rules.dictionary: exact membership in /usr/share/dict/words, confirmed afterwards with grep -x
admission: carried forward: every word of the existing NATURE bucket in data/aumlok-themes.json (the project own precedent)
definition engine: the word own dictionary gloss names a physical-world head noun within its first 12 tokens and no person/social/abstract head noun before it
definition recovery pass: same test with a 30-token window, applied only to the letters that could not otherwise reach the floor
compound engine: a dictionary word of 5-9 letters whose 4-9 letter tail is itself an admitted physical-world noun with a base of at least 4 letters
curated batches: words supplied by the lane author and then checked exactly against the dictionary
refusals: persons and social or institutional roles (the PEOPLE lane owns them)
religion, ritual, belief and mind (the SPIRIT lane owns them)
abstract nouns, and the morphology that marks them: -ness -tion -sion -ment -ism -ist -ity -ance -ence -ship -hood -less -able -ible -ward -wise
gerunds in -ing, past tenses in -ed (except physical descriptors such as winged, leaved, frosted), adverbs in -ly (except holly, lily, woolly and the like)
the v3 vocabulary ban: any word carrying the banned stem is dropped by rule and never named here, because the ban is itself a grep over this directory
